articles.title: Rising voice AI adoption creates new hiring demand for FDEs
articles.summary: Globally, job postings for Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) rose 729% year-on-year between April 2025 and April 2026, according to Indeed data. In India, postings surged 1,807% YoY in June 2026.

articles.summary: Hyderabad Police have launched Dooradrishti, an AI platform to profile accused persons and identify criminal networks, but questions remain about its data sources, accuracy and safeguards. articles.title: Helsing built an AI system that prepares targets for weapons systems and says every decision will carry a human name
articles.summary: Helsing has unveiled Clarity, an AI platform that uses agents to distill sensor data into target recommendations for weapons systems, all under human oversight and European control. But experience from the Iran war, Gaza, and a near-miss involving China shows that the speed of automation and data fusion create risks that are hard to contain. articles.title: Fewer hours and higher wages – or more burnout and surveillance: employers told to prepare for AI
articles.summary: Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launches best practice guide on AI adoption after Qantas and Canva job cutsGet our daily political email, free app or daily news podcastEntry-level jobs will be the first to be automated due to AI, but it could mean fewer hours and higher wages for ordinary workers – or make jobs tougher with more burnout and workplace surveillance – the government has warned employers.While major companies like Qantas and Canva slash their workforces in restructures spurred by AI changes, workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth said employers must give workers “a clear plan” about how automation could affect their jobs, and the opportunity to move into new roles.Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here Continue reading...
